findings.title: Off-by-one in `get`: `index <= items.len()` panics when index == len
`Sum_All` breaks Rust naming conventions and can be simplified

passes.answer:
The repo is a single-file Rust crate (`src/lib.rs`) with no existing tests, and the PR adds two functions: `get` and `Sum_All`. Review:

- **`get` is broken at the boundary.** The guard is `index <= items.len()`, so `index == items.len()` passes the check and then `items[index]` panics with "index out of bounds" instead of returning `None` — exactly the case the doc comment promises to handle. `items.get(index).copied()` (or a strict `<`) fixes it.
- **`Sum_All`** is functionally correct (the `as i64` cast prevents realistic overflow, since overflowing `i64` would take ~2³² max-value elements), but the name trips the default `non_snake_case` lint, and the manual index loop is unidiomatic.
- **No tests anywhere.** A one-line boundary test (`get(&[1,2], 2) == None`) would have caught the off-by-one.
